mutants.description: reg_file is instanced with its two magic key bytes swapped: DISABLE_KEY is set to the write-access value 0xA7 and WRITE_ACCESS_KEY to the disable value 0xD1
mutants.reason: The documented sequence, 0xD1 to DISABLE_KEY then CONTROL bit 0 cleared, no longer arms the disable, so spi_enable and En stay high. 0xD1 at 0x4F no longer unlocks the threshold bank, so a keyed threshold write sets write_rejected and leaves the thresholds unchanged.

mutants.description: The timestamp prescaler is handed PRESCALE_VAL minus one, an off-by-one 'fix' made at the call site although timestamp already compares its prescaler with PRESCALE_VAL-1
mutants.reason: The millisecond tick comes every 49999 clocks instead of 50000, so timestamp_ms runs fast by one clock per tick. TIME_0..2, the fault_time snapshot and the 5 s host watchdog drift, and a read near a tick boundary returns a count one higher than the true elapsed milliseconds.

after: logic latch_assert_q;   // strike_counter's latch_assert, before the output register
always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
mutants.description: latch_out is retimed through an extra output flop 'because it drives the SCR gate', though the header says it is driven straight from strike_counter's latch_assert
mutants.reason: On the hiccup entry that reaches the strike limit, latch_out rises one clock late. The supervisor, fault_cause and fault_LED, which all read latch_out, also see the CPLD's strike latch a clock later, so the Red_LED1 solid indication is a clock late too.

after: logic pwm_mask_out;   // pwm_mask's masked PWM, before the pin register
always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
mutants.description: The gate PWM gets a second pin register at the top level for glitch-free output, although pwm_mask's output is already a flop
mutants.reason: Both edges of every PWM_out pulse lag Osc_in by one more clock than designed. This includes the truncated edge where the on-time ceiling cuts a long pulse, so the gate drive runs one clock behind the modulator in S_SS and S_RUN.

mutants.description: spi_slave's SCK falling edge is taken straight from the unfiltered synchronised SCK, so only the rising (sampling) edge goes through the glitch filter, as if only the sample edge needed filtering
mutants.reason: sck_fall now comes 8 clocks earlier than the filtered rising edge, so MISO changes 160 ns earlier in each bit. A short low glitch on SCK during its high phase now makes a false fall and rise, which shifts an extra bit and corrupts the frame (CRC fail and txn_abort on a write, wrong read data).

mutants.description: reg_file's timestamp snapshot is only taken for reads that begin inside the TIME bank (0x18-0x1A), though rd_first must freeze it at the start of any read
mutants.reason: A burst read that starts below 0x18, for example at STATUS 0x10, and sweeps through 0x18-0x1A returns the snapshot left by an earlier read, or 0 after reset, instead of the current timestamp.

mutants.description: The dead-master SCK idle timeout is given the 5 s host-silence watchdog interval (WD_TIMEOUT_MS) instead of its own 2 ms
mutants.reason: If the master stops clocking with CS still low, the slave reaches S_DEAD only after 5 s, not 2 ms. During a read MISO keeps showing read data that long, and a stalled write is not poisoned in that time.

mutants.description: The switch-press pulse is qualified by the host enable, as if a host veto had to outrank the physical switch, so a press is ignored exactly when the host has disabled the converter
mutants.reason: After a keyed host disable, a fresh press of the enable switch no longer sets spi_enable. En stays low and the supervisor stays in S_OFF until the 5 s watchdog releases the veto.
